content:
Online media "胡‧說樓市" reported on Friday (2nd) that an over-$100 million detached house at One Stanley in Stanley has steel reinforcement quality issues, with analysis showing that the number of rebars in some areas is approximately 41% to 75% less than the approved plans. The Buildings Department stated on Saturday (3rd) that it had received a report and, after inspection, found that a beam on the ground floor did not have steel wire mesh in its protective layer as required by the plans, and the rebar configuration in some floor slabs did not match the plans. According to "胡‧說樓市", developer Kinson Properties had issued a legal letter requesting to suspend or stop the publication of the report, stating that "if unverified allegations affect the project's sales, we reserve the right to pursue legal liability." The vendor of One Stanley, Kin Wai Company Limited, issued a statement last night saying that it takes the matter very seriously and will follow up rigorously, and that if any rectification is found after investigation, it will definitely carry out remedial work for the affected properties in accordance with the law and pursue the responsibility of the persons concerned.

Developer: Kinson Properties　Contractor: Hoi Yuet Construction

128 Wong Ma Kok Road, Stanley, is a low-density luxury residence with only 82 units in the entire development, including 32 detached houses and 11 apartment blocks. The developer is Kinson Properties, and the contractor is Hoi Yuet Construction Engineering, a subsidiary of China State Construction Engineering (Hong Kong). Kinson Properties was established in 2013, founded by Lo Ka-kui and Lo Kin-yat, father and son, who are descendants of the Bossini family.

"胡‧說樓市" has been following the incident for over half a year and reported that the owner purchased the unit in April 2024, and during renovations in August, discovered that the surface concrete of some floor slabs was abnormal, with the plaster surface layer below the floor of the master bedroom on the second floor peeling off, and subsequently found that the rebars had shifted and had inconsistent spacing.

The report stated that after the Buildings Department carried out scanning and removal tests, the contractor's registered structural engineer, based on the Buildings Department's data analysis, pointed out that the number of main rebars in some parts of the study on the second floor was approximately 41% to 75% less than the approved plans; and in parts of the bedroom ceiling on the first floor, it was approximately 42% to 57.9% less.

Buildings Department issued occupation permit in July 2023

The Buildings Department responded to "胡‧說樓市"'s report, stating that it had received a report and had been following up on the investigation seriously. The Buildings Department pointed out that the detached house was granted an occupation permit in July 2023, and the owner carried out renovations after purchasing it. The Buildings Department received a report from the owner's representative in January this year regarding structural safety issues with the floor slabs in the house. After an on-site inspection in March, it was considered that the overall building structure did not pose an obvious danger. The department wrote to require the project's registered structural engineer to submit relevant material test reports and certificates.

Buildings Department: Rebar configuration in some floor slabs does not match plans

The Buildings Department stated that it had conducted multiple inspections from June to September this year, carrying out concrete strength rebound hammer tests, surface thickness gauge surveys, surface radar surveys of rebar configuration, core drilling compressive tests, and on-site excavation inspections, and is analyzing the data. The Buildings Department stated that tests and inspections found that the protective layer of a beam on the ground floor of the detached house did not have steel wire mesh configured as per the plans; in addition, the rebar configuration in some floor slabs did not match the plans.

Written to developer and others requesting assistance with investigation

The Buildings Department pointed out that these situations "do not constitute an obvious danger" and will be further investigated. The department has written to the project's developer, contractor, authorized person, and registered structural engineer, requesting assistance with the investigation. The Buildings Department reminded the industry that, according to the Buildings Ordinance, construction professionals and contractors must supervise and carry out construction in accordance with the approved plans. The department also pointed out that if the investigation finds that construction professionals and contractors have violated the Buildings Ordinance, it will definitely take serious follow-up action, including prosecution and/or initiating disciplinary action.

Vendor: Will make a statement at an appropriate time after gathering and verifying more information

The vendor of One Stanley, Kin Wai Company Limited, responded that it takes the matter very seriously and will follow up rigorously. The company stated that, based on information released by the Buildings Department, the Buildings Department considers that the overall building structure of the property does not pose an obvious danger. Kin Wai stated that it is currently understanding and verifying the details in detail, and will do its best to cooperate with the Buildings Department's investigation, and will make a statement at an appropriate time after gathering and verifying more information. If any rectification is found after investigation regarding any person's construction quality or other related matters, it will definitely carry out remedial work for the affected properties in accordance with laws and regulations, and pursue the responsibility of the persons concerned in accordance with the law.
